summary: A president addresses listeners across the country without assuming they all live in the player’s town.
realLife: At Kentucky Dam in 1945, Harry Truman began with Roosevelt’s earlier dam dedication and then told his audience why the Tennessee Valley project belonged to people throughout the country.
inGame: The inaugural outline selects the national occasion and its address parts.
gates: The speaker is giving the national address.

turns.what: The president names the host town before turning to people listening around the country.
turns.pulledBy: The address has both a local audience and a national broadcast.
turns.writesBack: The opening distinguishes the venue from the reach of the address.

turns.what: A station outside the valley joins the address after the dedication and carries the passage about who paid for the work.
turns.pulledBy: Its broadcast log gives the time the national feed replaced the local program.
turns.writesBack: The station’s news recap draws on the portion its listeners heard.
